name: sql-private-endpoint
displayName: SQL Server VM with Private Blob Storage
description: SQL Server 2022 Developer on a private Windows VM with Azure Bastion administration and Blob Storage reachable only through a private endpoint.
what: A private SQL Server lab environment built on a Windows VM. The VM has no public IP, administrators connect through Azure Bastion, and a StorageV2 account exposes Blob only through Private Link. Private DNS resolves the Blob endpoint inside the VNet, and the VM managed identity receives Storage Blob Data Contributor access.
why: SQL Server workloads often need private object storage for backups, imports, exports, and data exchange. This use case demonstrates private network connectivity and identity-based authorization without exposing either the VM or Blob endpoint to the public internet.
potentialUseCases: SQL Server backup and restore testing with private Azure Blob Storage
Migration labs for SQL Server workloads that require private object storage
Private Link and DNS validation from an infrastructure VM
Non-production testing of SQL Server 2022 managed identity access to Blob

reliability: Premium managed OS disk provides durable VM storage
Production profile uses zone-redundant Blob storage
Private DNS integration provides stable Blob endpoint resolution
security: The SQL Server VM has no public IP and is administered through Azure Bastion
Blob public network access and shared-key authorization are disabled
The VM uses a managed identity and scoped Blob data-plane RBAC
Trusted Launch enables Secure Boot and vTPM
costOptimization: SQL Server Developer edition has no SQL license charge and is restricted to non-production use
Development uses a smaller D2s v5 VM and locally redundant storage
VM shutdown schedules can reduce compute cost when the lab is idle
operationalExcellence: Bicep and Terraform implementations provide repeatable deployments
SQL IaaS Agent registration enables Azure SQL VM management features
Dev and prod profiles make sizing and storage redundancy explicit
performanceEfficiency: Dsv5 VM sizes can be changed as SQL workload demand grows
Private Link keeps Blob traffic on the Microsoft backbone
Dedicated workload, private endpoint, and Bastion subnets isolate network roles

quota.summary: Requires regional Dsv5-family VM quota and availability for the selected SQL Server marketplace image and Azure Bastion.

requirements.detail: The subscription needs sufficient Standard Dsv5 Family vCPU quota in the selected region.

architecture.summary: Administrators reach a private SQL Server VM through Azure Bastion. The VM resolves and accesses Blob Storage through a private endpoint using its managed identity.

components.name: SQL Server VM (D4s v5, Windows)
components.notes: One always-on Windows VM. SQL Server Developer edition is license-free for non-production use only. OS disk charges are excluded.

components.name: Azure Bastion (Standard)
components.notes: One continuously provisioned Standard Bastion host.

components.name: Azure Private Endpoint
components.notes: One Blob private endpoint. Data processing is usage-based and excluded.

components.name: Blob storage capacity
components.notes: Example assumes 100 GB of Blob data. Transactions and retrieval charges are excluded.

components.name: Public IP (Standard, static)
components.notes: One static public IP used only by Azure Bastion.
